title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A/S is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over a base of characteristic p. The page continues the 'N.B.' of the previous page, which constructed canonical isomorphisms between the sheaves L_A, L_{A*} and the duals of the étale parts of pA*, pA. Those isomorphisms hold over the ordinary locus, where they give the tangent spaces an F_p-structure.

Step 1. Define the Hodge line bundle ω_A = det(t_A)^{-1} = Λ^g t_A^∨ (the transcription's t_A^* means the dual).

Step 2. Where A is ordinary, ω_A comes with an F_p-structure: a locally constant invertible F_p-sheaf, namely the determinant of (pA*)_ét (or its dual). This sheaf tensored over F_p with O_S gives ω_A. The key elementary remark: if a line bundle L is X ⊗_{F_p} O_S for an invertible F_p-sheaf X, then L^{⊗(p-1)} has a canonical nowhere-vanishing section. Locally take a generator x of X and form x^{⊗(p-1)}. This is independent of x, because (ax)^{p-1} = a^{p-1} x^{p-1} = x^{p-1} for a in F_p^*. Hence ω_A^{⊗(p-1)} is canonically trivialized on the ordinary locus.

Step 3. Let U ⊂ S be the open set of points s with A_s ordinary. Applying Step 2 to A|U gives a canonical section σ of ω^{⊗(p-1)} over U, nowhere zero. A crossed-out attempt tried to extend σ from a relatively dense U to S as a pseudo-section; Grothendieck abandons it.

Step 4. Instead he defines the extension directly on all of S. Take the linear map π: t_A^{(p)} → t_A. This is Lie(V) for the Verschiebung V: A^{(p)} → A, equivalently the linearization of the p-operation X ↦ X^{[p]} on the restricted Lie algebra. Taking determinants gives (det t_A)^{⊗p} → det t_A, i.e. a global section σ_A of (det t_A)^{1-p} = ω_A^{⊗(p-1)}.

Step 5 (next page). σ_A is named the Hasse invariant of A. Its zero locus is exactly the non-ordinary locus. A canonical isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} is deduced from the Hodge filtration of DR^1(A/S) and the trivialization DR^{2g}(A/S) ≅ O_S. It is claimed compatible with the p-structures, so it sends σ_A to σ_{A*} and, when A is ordinary, gives det(pA)_ét ≅ det(pA*)_ét.

The problem served: constructing the Hasse invariant intrinsically, for abelian schemes of any dimension over any base, and relating it to the étale/F_p-structure on the ordinary locus. This belongs to Grothendieck's 1969 study of Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals.
errors: The page writes ω_A^{(p-1)}; this means the tensor power ω_A^{⊗(p-1)}, not a Frobenius twist.

The page does not check that the Step-4 section σ_A restricts on U to the Step-2 section built from the F_p-structure (possibly up to a sign or convention). This is true: on the ordinary locus the F_p-structure is the fixed-point sheaf of the p-linear map on the tangent space. But it is left implicit.
The letter 'L' in mid-page stands for ω_A (or the relevant line bundle); the notation is inconsistent with the first line.

ideas.what: Hasse invariant of an abelian scheme as the determinant of Lie(V): t_A^{(p)} → t_A, a section of ω^{⊗(p-1)} whose zero locus is the non-ordinary locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hasse and Deuring (elliptic curves); Hasse–Witt matrix; modern form in Katz (1973), Serre, Katz–Mazur, Faltings–Chai

ideas.what: An invertible F_p-local system on the ordinary locus gives a canonical trivialization of ω^{⊗(p-1)} via x ↦ x^{p-1}; the Hasse invariant extends it to all of S
ideas.modern_name: Relation between the Hasse invariant and the Igusa cover (the Hasse invariant is a (p-1)-th power on the Igusa tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Igusa; Serre and Katz (1972–73, Antwerp III); Gross (1990, tameness criterion)

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism ω_A ≅ ω_{A*} via the Hodge filtration and DR^{2g} ≅ O_S, compatible with Hasse invariants
ideas.modern_name: Equality of Hodge bundles and Hasse invariants of an abelian scheme and its dual

missed.claim: Around 1969 Grothendieck gives an intrinsic construction of the Hasse invariant of an abelian scheme of arbitrary dimension. He explicitly interprets it as the extension, from the ordinary locus, of the canonical section of ω^{⊗(p-1)} coming from an F_p-structure (the determinant of the étale part of pA*). This slightly predates the standard published treatments of Katz and Serre (1972–73), but the content is now standard. It is a priority detail, not a new result.
missed.quote: À ce titre, ω_A^{⊗(p-1)} admet une section canonique.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it documents Grothendieck's independent formulation of the Hasse invariant via p-structures in his Barsotti–Tate notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is correct and elegant, but the Hasse invariant as a section of ω^{p-1}, and its relation to the étale F_p-structure on the ordinary locus, are standard (Katz, Serre, Igusa tower). Only a small historical priority interest remains.
transcription_corrections: The first formula should read ω_A = det(t_A)^{-1} = Λ^g t_A^∨ (dual), not 'A det'.

The middle passage likely reads roughly: 'Si A/S ordinaire ... plus généralement soit U l'ouvert des s tels que A_s est ordinaire; ce qui précède s'applique à A|U, en particulier on trouve une section canonique σ de L|U, partout ≠ 0'.
The final formula is σ_A ∈ Γ((det t_A)^{1-p}) = Γ(ω_A^{⊗(p-1)}).
In the line 'on a un faisceau inv. ... sur F_p', what is meant is an invertible F_p-sheaf (an F_p-structure) on the ordinary locus, namely det((pA*)_ét).
